Company Profile

{{company.name}} is a Dubai-based freight forwarding and logistics company. We help importers, exporters and traders move cargo between the UAE and the world by sea, air and road, and we look after the paperwork, customs clearance and delivery that sit around every shipment.

Who we are

We are a focused team that answers its own phone. Every customer has a named coordinator who knows the shipment, speaks to the carrier and tells you early when something changes. We keep our service simple: a clear quotation, a confirmed booking, regular updates and an invoice that matches what we quoted.

What we do

ServiceWhat it covers
Ocean freightFCL and LCL import, export and cross-trade; booking, container release, documentation, tracking.
Air freightAirport-to-airport and door-to-door; consolidation, charter enquiries, time-critical cargo.
Road transportUAE trucking and GCC cross-border movements; trip planning and proof of delivery.
Customs clearanceImport and export declarations, duty and document preparation with licensed customs brokers.
WarehousingReceiving, storage, picking, dispatch and stock reporting for customer-owned cargo.
Project and special cargoOut-of-gauge, temperature-sensitive and dangerous goods handled with qualified carriers and the required declarations.

How we work

  • One coordinator per customer account, reachable by phone and e-mail.
  • Written quotation before booking; changes confirmed in writing.
  • Milestone updates from booking to proof of delivery, available through our tracking portal.
  • Monthly statements and a named contact in accounts.

1. Confidential information

“Confidential Information” means any non-public information that one party (the Discloser) gives to the other (the Recipient) in connection with the Purpose, in any form, including customer and supplier lists, rates, shipment data, pricing, business plans, systems and documents marked or reasonably understood to be confidential.

2. Obligations

  1. Use Confidential Information only for the Purpose.
  2. Keep it secret with at least the care used for its own confidential information, and disclose it only to employees and advisers who need it and are bound by similar duties.
  3. Not copy it except as needed for the Purpose.

3. Exceptions

These obligations do not apply to information that is public through no fault of the Recipient, was already lawfully known to the Recipient, is independently developed, or must be disclosed by law or order of a competent authority (the Recipient will give prompt notice where permitted).

4. Return or destruction

On request or when the Purpose ends, the Recipient will return or destroy Confidential Information and confirm in writing.

5. Term

This agreement lasts [2] years from the effective date. Confidentiality obligations continue for [3] years after it ends or for as long as the information remains confidential, whichever is longer.

6. General

No licence or partnership is created. Neither party must proceed with any transaction. Template Use and Company Setup Guide

1. Set up once

  1. Open ELV-001 and ELV-008 and enter the registered address, trade licence number, issuing authority and VAT TRN (if registered).
  2. Enter bank beneficiary name, bank and IBAN on the invoice templates (ELV-023 to ELV-029) after Finance has verified them.
  3. List authorised signatories and approval limits in ELV-006 (Company Resolution).
  4. Agree the standard terms with your legal adviser and insert them in ELV-014, ELV-021 and ELV-022.

2. Using a template

  1. Open the DOTX in Word to create a new document, or copy the DOCX.
  2. Replace every bracketed field. Delete unused rows and guidance notes.
  3. Save with the reference number in the file name, e.g. ELV-023-INV-2026-0001.docx.
  4. Export to PDF for customers; keep the editable copy internally.

3. Numbering

DocumentSuggested formatOwner
QuotationELV-Q-YYYY-NNNSales
BookingELV-BK-YYYY-NNNOperations
InvoiceSequential, no gaps (as required for tax invoices)Accounts
Purchase orderELV-PO-YYYY-NNNProcurement
ClaimELV-CLM-YYYY-NNNOperations

4. Review before issue

  • Customer, company and shipment details are correct.
  • Units, currency, dates (DD MMM YYYY) and time zone (GST) are stated.
  • Totals and VAT are checked – these templates do not calculate.
  • Approvals and signatures are obtained.
  • The document is archived under its reference.

5. What these templates are not

  • They are not carrier, customs or authority forms. Use the current official documents where required.
  • A company letter is not a carrier release order.
  • Contracts are starting points; have your legal adviser approve them.
  • Employment summaries support HR administration and do not replace official employment contracts.
  • Tax fields follow FTA invoice guidance; Finance decides registration, place of supply, VAT rate and e-invoicing obligations.

6. Reference sources

  • FTA Tax Invoices clarification VATP006: https://tax.gov.ae/DataFolder/Files/Pdf/06-Tax-Invoices.pdf

Standard Trading Conditions

Terms on which the company provides freight forwarding and logistics services. Attach to quotations and the customer account form.

Guidance: this is an editable starting text, not legal advice. Have it reviewed by the company’s legal adviser before use, and keep the signed copy under the reference number.

1. Definitions

“Company” means {{company.name}}. “Customer” means the person who requests the services, and anyone acting for them. “Goods” means the cargo and its packing. “Services” means freight forwarding, transport, customs, warehousing and related services.

2. Quotations and bookings

Quotations are valid for the period stated and are subject to carrier space, equipment and surcharges at the time of booking. A booking is accepted when the Company confirms it in writing. Rates exclude duties, taxes, demurrage, detention and storage unless stated.

3. Customer’s obligations

  • Give complete and accurate information about the Goods, including description, weight, volume, value, HS code and any dangerous or restricted nature.
  • Pack, mark and label the Goods suitably for the journey.
  • Provide the documents needed by carriers, customs and other authorities on time.
  • Confirm that the Goods are lawful to ship and are not subject to sanctions or export restrictions.

4. Dangerous, perishable and special goods

Dangerous, temperature-controlled, valuable, out-of-gauge and other special Goods are accepted only after the Customer has declared them and the carrier has approved the booking. The Customer is responsible for all consequences of incorrect or missing declarations.

5. Customs

The Company acts on the Customer’s instructions and through licensed customs brokers where required. The Customer remains responsible for the accuracy of declarations, duties, taxes, fines and charges.

6. Carriers and subcontractors

The Company may use carriers and subcontractors it selects. Their terms, including bills of lading and air waybills, apply to the carriage.

7. Liability

[State the Company’s limits of liability per kilogram or per shipment, the notice period for claims, and the exclusions for delay and indirect loss, after review by the Company’s legal adviser and insurer.]

8. Insurance

The Company does not insure the Goods unless the Customer instructs it in writing and the premium is paid. The Customer is advised to insure the Goods for their full value.

9. Payment

Invoices are payable by the due date stated, in the currency stated, without set-off. The Company may charge [rate] on overdue amounts and suspend credit and release of cargo until all amounts are paid.

10. Lien

The Company has a lien on the Goods and on any documents for all sums due from the Customer, and may sell the Goods after reasonable notice to recover them.

11. Force majeure

Neither party is liable for failure caused by events beyond its reasonable control, including war, strikes, port congestion, weather, pandemic and government action.

12. Governing law

These conditions are governed by the laws of the United Arab Emirates as applied in the Emirate of Dubai. Disputes are referred to [the Dubai courts / arbitration at …].
